evidence_loop.label: the assurance plane, and the first verdict it returned
evidence_loop.summary: ADR-0053 separated three facts the baseline had collapsed into one word: whether the observed host tuple matches exactly, whether a human reviewer accepted this host pair against this installed code, and whether the record is structurally intact. ADR-0054 settled the three questions it deferred — the record schema, the doctor report version (measured: it does NOT bump, because bumping makes every retained artifact malformed while buying nothing the nested result version already provides), and where the minimum runtime floor lives. Eight slices built the plane bottom-up: record schema and structural reader, packaged host-version comparator and direction vocabulary, the semantic matcher (membership, cohort, package binding, negative-wins, tombstone), doctor's three-layer verdict, compat's frozen observation, and both readiness paths gating on assurance. An adversarial audit then enumerated the reachable false-assurance paths and closed them, including the mirrors the first fix left. This record is authored for the loop's first operator-visible verdict, and that verdict is a REFUSAL: R1 ships with no grants, so every host reads unassured and readiness is gated shut.

feature_commits.note: ADR-0053. Splits the baseline's single freshness word into exactness, assurance and integrity, and states the failure mode so it cannot be traded away: loosening the verdict risks missing a real contract change in a host surface this framework consumes. Deferred three questions to a follow-up.

ADR-0054. Settles all three deferred questions plus three the list had treated as implementation detail and which turned out to be safety properties: where the floor lives, what the packaged comparator is, and how the non-resurrection clause holds. The doctor version deliberately does NOT bump.
The assurance record: schema, baseline section, and structural reader. Lands with no active grant by design — the reader must be shippable before anything it reads exists.
Packaged host-version comparator and direction vocabulary, so a drift can be reported as ahead/behind/exact rather than only as changed. Single-sourced into CI.

The semantic matcher — membership, cohort, package binding, negative-wins, tombstone gate. Still no grant: matching is separated from granting so the matcher can be reviewed before it can ever return a positive.
Doctor reports integrity, exactness and assurance as three facts rather than one, with the report schema migration and the consumer contract. Not yet a gate.
Compat OBSERVES assurance at snapshot time and freezes the verdict into the snapshot; check projects it and never re-evaluates, so a remembered snapshot can never be retroactively granted assurance.
Both readiness paths gate on assurance, and the minimum runtime floor. This is the commit that makes the refusal reachable by an operator.

hardening_commits.note: Adversarial audit of the assembled plane: enumerates the reachable false-assurance paths and closes them, including the mirrors the first fix left. The mirror clause is the finding — a fix that covered one of two duplicated paths would have shipped the other.

install_method: No install was performed by this loop: both hosts were already on 0.91.1 when the recovery began, having been updated by the operator after release. The installed state rests on the doctor read plus the four-way byte comparison recorded under readings; no runtime:settings --execute-plugin-management executor artifact was produced.
narrative:
Authored in the post-release position ADR-0049 requires: the tags, squashes, marketplace-sync shas, proof run id and artifact hash exist only after the implementation PRs merged, release-please cut #704 and #711, the catalog syncs landed, and the proof was re-recorded against the installed 0.91.1.

The reading that matters is a REFUSAL, and it is the designed outcome rather than a defect. ADR-0053 §Decision 6 asked for the gate's rejection path to be observed on a real machine before the plane could be trusted; this proof is that observation. R1 ships with an empty grant list by owner decision (2026-08-17), so the matcher can only return unassured, every host reads unassured, and readiness is gated shut. The next step doctor prints is deliberately not an action the operator can take alone — assurance is granted by human review of this host pair against this installed code, not by a version match, an upgrade, or elapsed time. The first grant is a separate forward-patch loop; it could not have ridden along here even in principle, because this recovery is forbidden from editing the protected baseline the grant would live in.

The parity number moved in two directions at once and must not be read as a single trend. Earned weight went UP, 105/115 to 106/130: the previous loop's two partials were one operator action (a Codex /hooks review after all four hook-bearing packages bumped), and that action was completed on 2026-08-16 as settings-20260816T233407Z-4f23d9 — after that loop's proof was taken, which is why the stage docs carried a 91% 6/8 reading that the machine had already moved past. Both criteria now read satisfied with zero manual follow-ups. The percentage nonetheless FELL to 82% because the denominator grew: host_compatibility_assurance is a ninth criterion introduced by this very release, and it is worth 15 of which an unassured host earns 6. A record that reported only the percentage would have described this release as a regression when what actually happened is that a new fact started being measured.

The one blocked criterion is this loop's own measurement, not a fault it inherited. runtime_handoff_artifacts reads blocked because the mandated host re-measurement took a fresh compat snapshot and Claude had moved 2.1.233 to 2.1.234, so the run legitimately reports release_notes_required. Closing it means ingesting content-backed release notes and then refreshing the packaged baseline — which is a protected runtime asset, and editing it here would start a new release obligation and manufacture another release-and-recovery lap. That is R2 work by construction. This is also the third consecutive loop to land on a baseline the host had already passed, which is the cost datum ADR-0052 measured (3 of 12 loops land current) rather than a new surprise.

One scope note worth preserving for the next author. The proof-coupled documentation tokens could not be synced until this narrative was written, because sync-doc-versions refuses to bump a version that sits beside a stale proof citation. That ordering is deliberate and it worked as designed here: the refusal names the run id it expects, so the only way to satisfy the script is to have actually read the new proof.
